rationale: The complete unit:given.patterns introduces binding pattern b with variable and flat class/field-to-variable alternatives. Its selected Unique/Unpacking.Pattern and Statement have exactly these alternatives and pair a pattern with the unchanged Unique.Value; Configuration contains the extended statement list and the same storage state. unit:given.classes introduces C, f and the field count n, and unit:given.syntax introduces x, p, e and t, so the grammar and give-versus-pattern explanation have defined notation. Source shorthand f for f:f is a presentation abbreviation of the field/name pair, not an additional evaluator form. I inspected the captured full Unpacking module for the behavioral sentences: Transfer selects/removes one matching field per pair and succeeds at its empty base case only when no fields remain; Bind.unpack also requires distinct field names, distinct variable names, and freshness. Thus all declaration fields occur exactly once in any order, and a fieldless object admits the empty pattern. Bind.unpack deletes the consumed container, while Unique.Take.field only clears a field and keeps the container. Pattern contains no recursive pattern, wildcard or rest alternative. Expression evaluation is literally reused, and embed_step/reflect_step state preservation of old single-variable behavior, with reflection allowing an arbitrary extended successor. The preservation result described as following this introduction is confined to structural well-formedness. No undefined notation or mismatched syntactic/semantic distinction was found.
limitations: This is a source correspondence review, not execution of Lean, Cargo, rendering or evidence validation. Lean is responsible for proof correctness; tactic bodies were not independently re-proved.
